newsitem.title: NORWAY: Six Swedish, Norwegian banks to present Q1 profits.
newsitem.headline: Six Swedish, Norwegian banks to present Q1 profits.

text.p: Six Swedish and Norwegian banks will present first-quarter profits on Tuesday amid merger talk and takeover battles in their sector.
Norway's largest insurance company Storebrand ASA will also report profits for the first quarter.

Sweden's Nordbanken and S-E-Banken are both expected to show an increase in operating profits after credit losses, according to analysts' forecasts compiled by Reuters. No forecast was made for Foreningsbanken.
Norway's Den norske Bank (DnB), Christiania Bank og Kreditkasse and Union Bank of Norway (UBN) were all expected to book lower profits.
"Interest margins have been falling in Norway for three years and are still not at the floor," said James Alexander, a banking analyst at Dresdner Kleinwort Benson in London.

"It is to do with excessive competition in Norway, while in Sweden there is a more disciplined banking market. Swedish banks don't price deposits or loans at a level that would not yield an adequate return on equity to an institutional investor."
In Norway, volume is growing, but revenue is flat, he said.
On the other hand, analysts do not believe Swedish banks will continue to increase profits long-term because loan losses cannot keep falling for ever.
An Oslo-based financial analyst agreed competition was more intensive in Norway. "You have more and smaller banks in Norway, while in Sweden they are becoming bigger and fewer," he said.
Analysts target a nine percent rise in Nordbanken's earnings to 1.70 billion Swedish crowns ($217 million) and a two percent increase in S-E-Banken's profit to 1.38 billion.
The two banks are expected to resume the merger talks they broke off earlier this year.

Speculation about a Swedish bank merger flurry took off last autumn and since then Handelsbanken has taken over mortgage lender Stadshypotek, and Swedbank and Foreningsbanken have announced plans to merge.
These moves have put further pressure on Nordbanken and S-E-Banken, the two remaining large banks in Sweden's financial sector, to act.

The latest rumour says S-E-Banken could be split down the middle into investment and retail banking before the latter is merged with Nordbanken. The investment banking operations could then be merged with a large foreign player, analysts said.
In Oslo, Storebrand moved forward its profits announcement by two weeks because of its planned merger with Christiania Bank, Norway's second largest bank.

The new company, Christiania Group, would have a market capitalisation of 26 billion Norwegian crowns. The merger, if approved by shareholders and authorities, would form the country's largest financial group and the sixth biggest in the Nordic region.

Christiania Bank was seen registering operating profits after loan losses of 494 million Norwegian crowns, down 12 percent. Storebrand was forecast to book group results of 288 million crowns, up 17 percent.

For UBN, Norway's top savings bank, operating profits after loan losses were forecast to drop 14 percent to 346 million Norwegian crowns. DnB, the country's biggest bank, was expected to book operating profits after loan losses of 698 million crowns, down 11 percent.
DnB is battling Fokus Bank, Norway's fourth biggest bank, for niche mortgage lender BNbank.

The situation at Fokus is complicated by a hostile takeover bid launched for it by Sparebankgruppen, a group of 16 savings banks seeking to carve it up. Fokus is hoping that a foreign bank, possibly Handelsbanken, may make a counterbid, according to analysts.

Handelsbanken gave the first indication of the health of the fast-changing Swedish banking sector on April 21 when it reported operating profit after credit losses rising 14 percent to 1.73 billion Swedish crowns in the first three months, beating market expectations.
